To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we used a multi-stage approach to develop an arts-based asthma knowledge translation tool, “My Asthma diary” and (2) we encountered specific challenges in this process that are worth considering when developing similar patient-driven knowledge translation tools.

the development of patient-driven knowledge translation tools is a rigorous process that requires the input of a diverse team and that there are challenges that must be considered when developing such tools.

we developed an arts-based knowledge translation strategy that was informed by parents' information needs on asthma and quality research evidence on asthma, that we encountered challenges in working in an interdisciplinary team, in the quantity and ordering of the information in the eBooks and in creating composite narratives, and in balancing the presentation of actual and ideal management of asthma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of patient-driven, creative tools for knowledge translation.
the process of developing a patient-driven arts and health knowledge translation tool.
the development and testing of an arts-based knowledge translation strategy for parents of children with childhood asthma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper describes a process exemplar for developing an innovative knowledge translation strategy that leverages the power of arts-based approaches to communicate health information and support illness self-management.
we describe the development of a patient-driven, arts-based knowledge translation approach that can be replicated for use with different patient populations and health contexts.
this paper reports on a process for developing a creative knowledge translation tool for parents, and describes the challenges encountered during this development process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a patient-driven knowledge translation tool, and we have developed a process for developing patient-driven knowledge translation tools.
we were able to use a multi-staged, trans-disciplinary process to develop an arts-based knowledge translation strategy that is tailored to the needs of parents of a child with asthma.
the process of developing “My Asthma Dairy” has been iterative, trans-disciplinary, and rigorous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
patient-driven knowledge translation is feasible and can be developed using an iterative process that is grounded in rigorous research evidence and patient-centered information needs.
the process of developing creative knowledge translation tools is as important as the final product, and that the process should be informed by a rigorous, multi-staged approach.
the development process for arts-based, patient-driven knowledge tools should be iterative, collaborative, and informed by research evidence and the needs of end-users.
